summary: Iteration 2 testing focused on the 3 new features: (1) user invite system (direct + email modes, RBAC for admin/manager), (2) Resend email integration, (3) atomic invoice/PO counters. Extended backend_test.py from 19 to 35 tests, all passing. Found and fixed 1 critical bug in GET /api/users/invitations/{token} - a Python operator-precedence bug in the expiry check that caused EVERY invitation token to be rejected as 'expired', completely blocking the accept-invite frontend flow. Frontend testing verified: Users page, Invite User modal (mode toggle hides/shows temp_password field), direct create user appears in table, /accept-invite shows 'Invalid Invitation' error for bad tokens, Team & Roles nav present under Operations sidebar, inline role selectors render per user.

critical.issue: FIXED. Operator-precedence bug at server.py:747 caused all invitations to return 410 'Invitation expired' because the ternary was evaluated before the outer if (datetime object is truthy). Replaced with explicit tz normalization. All invite-accept flows now work end-to-end.

issues: Recharts ResponsiveContainer logs width(-1)/height(-1) warning on first paint (carried over from iteration 1, non-blocking).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to ~1145 lines and now includes user invite/management routes too. Split into routers/ (auth, users, crm, erp, payments, email) is strongly recommended before adding more modules.

send_email uses asyncio.to_thread on a sync Resend client - acceptable but a background task would be more robust for invite flows (currently the API call waits on email send, which can stall response by 100-300ms).

invite_user (mode=invite) creates the pending user FIRST, then sends email. If Resend rejects (e.g., sandbox-mode email blocked), the user still exists in pending status. This is intentional per agent-context note (token is stored even if email fails) but worth documenting in API responses (e.g., return {warning: 'email_blocked'}).

accept_invitation doesn't re-validate that user.status is 'pending' before activating. Edge case: if admin pre-creates a 'direct' active user with the same email after sending an invite, the email index would block this anyway, so currently safe — but defensive check is cheap.
Cookie `secure=False` still set on accept_invitation (line 795) — consistent with login/register, fine for preview, must be env-driven for prod.
VALID_ROLES uses ['admin','manager','sales','user'] but there is no enum / DB constraint; relies purely on the API check. OK for blueprint.

rca of the issue: GET /api/users/invitations/{token} bug RCA: The expiry check was written as `if inv['expires_at'].replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if inv['expires_at'].tzinfo is None else inv['expires_at'] < datetime.now(timezone.utc):`. Python operator precedence binds the ternary tighter than the outer `if`, so it evaluates to: `if (datetime_obj if tzinfo_is_none else bool):`. Motor returns naive datetimes (tzinfo=None) so the ternary always returned the datetime object — a truthy value — making the outer `if` always True, always raising 410. Reproduction: create invite, GET /api/users/invitations/{token} → 410 even for fresh tokens. Fix: extract expiry into a variable, normalize tz first, then compare. Verified: TestUserInvite::test_invite_accept_with_real_token now passes; frontend AcceptInvitePage will now correctly fetch and accept real invitations.
